About Langley Castle | Learn All About Langley Castle Hotel
Skip to content
Romantic Getaways, Historic Breaks, and Fine Dining in Northumberland
About Langley Castle Hotel
Langley Castle Hotel is a 14th-century medieval castle nestled in the picturesque South Tyne Valley in Northumberland. Steeped in history and surrounded by ten acres of private gardens and woodland, Langley Castle offers a unique retreat for romantic getaways, castle weddings, and fine dining experiences.
With walls up to seven feet thick, this medieval castle provides a peaceful escape from the modern world. Inside, you'll find nine individually styled rooms within the main Castle - featuring four poster beds, window seats set into ancient stone, spa baths, saunas, and original fireplaces. An additional 19 dog-friendly luxury rooms are located just a short walk in Castle View, many of which enjoy stunning views of the Castle and are ideal for families or longer stays.
Dine in our award-winning restaurant, offering a refined menu that showcases local ingredients. For special occasions, private dining is available in the Pavilion (up to 30 guests), or in the Stuart Suite for banquet-style events of up to 120 guests.
Whether you're exploring Hadrian’s Wall, Vindolanda, or Northumberland National Park, or simply soaking up the Castle’s rich heritage, Langley Castle Hotel is where history, luxury, and memorable moments meet.
Awards
Langley Castle has earned numerous accolades over the years, including:
Awarded 4 stars from the AA and VisitEngland with a Gold Award
Multiple-Time Winner of Best Small Hotel of the Year – North East England
Best Hotel for Romance UK – 2018
Small Hotel of the Year (Silver) – 2022
Gold Award for Resilience and Innovation ​​ ​when coming out of lockdown – 2023
Highly Commended Hotel – 2023
Award-Winning Dining
In Northumberland
Step inside our 14th-century castle and discover a dining experience that’s full of character and charm. Our award-winning restaurants serve beautifully crafted dishes that bring together the best of classic and modern cuisine. Each seasonal menu is inspired by Northumberland’s finest local produce, from slow-cooked meats that simply melt in the mouth to freshly caught fish paired with flavours that perfectly complement each other.
You can choose from three distinctive settings to suit your mood. Enjoy an intimate, candle-lit dinner surrounded by centuries of history, dine in the contemporary Glass Pavilion with its elegant, modern design, or unwind in the Drawing Room, a cosy space for afternoon tea or a quiet nightcap.
Book Your Table
Fairy Tale Weddings
At Langley Castle Hotel
Set amid the picturesque Northumberland countryside, Langley Castle Hotel offers a romantic historic backdrop and a choice of grand spaces for your dream fairy-tale wedding. Beloved by couples from around the world, our team is dedicated to creating celebrations as unique and personal as each love story. From intimate elopements to grand, exclusive occasions, making you feel like royalty for a day.
From the grandeur of the Stuart Suite at the top of the castle, with breath-taking views of the Northumberland countryside through large arched stained-glass windows and the soft glow of a sparkling chandelier, to the historic charm of the Drawing Room, featuring high-beamed ceilings, exposed 7-foot-thick stone walls, rich red-patterned carpets, and opulent furnishings, Langley Castle Hotel offers unforgettable ceremony settings. Say “I do” beneath a soaring arched window that casts a natural spotlight on your most treasured moment.
For those dreaming of an outdoor wedding, our enchanting woodland spaces offer a fairy-tale backdrop, perfect for spring and summer ceremonies, where you’ll be surrounded by flourishing landscapes and birdsong on your special day.
Email Our Wedding Team
Battlements Tours
Langley Castle  is an exceptionally authentic English castle, complete with over 670 years of history, since it was first built in 1350. This rich heritage, and the genuine fortifications that the castle boasts, not to mention its medieval garderobes (the best in Europe), all demand exploration, which is why we offer guests – and non-residents too – our daily ‘Battlements Tour’.
Taking place just after breakfast has finished being served, the tour will open your eyes to parts of Langley Castle that may have escaped your attention as a guest or visitor, as well as being your passport into the rich history of the castle and the personalities who have called it home.
Do not miss out on the opportunity to join the tour, if you can.
Discover more
The History of Langley Castle Hotel
At Langley Castle, our history dates back to 1350, during the reign of Edward III. The castle has retained its architectural integrity and is considered one of the few medieval fortified castle hotels in England. Over the past 600 years, it and its estate have been owned by Lords and Ladies whose names were often intertwined with the turbulent history of the kingdom.
To learn more, read the full history below.

Scenic Things to do in Northumberland | Langley Castle Hotel
Skip to content
14th Century Medieval Castle in Northumberland
The History of Langley Castle
Tucked away in the quiet countryside village of Langley, Northumberland, England, Langley Castle holds over 670 years of history within its stone walls. Built in 1350 during the reign of Edward III, the castle was granted to Sir Thomas de Lucy, a loyal knight who constructed it to secure his estate and defend it against the turbulent times of war. Its strong stone walls, high towers, and strategic location made it both a symbol of power and a fortress.
Our comprehensive history guide traces the Castle’s lineage from its 14th-century origins to the present day. Discover its connections to key moments in British history, explore the evolution of its purpose over the centuries, and uncover many more fascinating insights into its rich past.
The Legacy of Langley Castle
Langley Castle has preserved its architectural integrity for centuries, one of England’s few medieval fortified castle hotels still in original form. In the 17th century, the Earls of Derwentwater inherited it. James Radcliffe and his brother Charles supported their cousin, James Edward Stuart, in the 1715 Jacobite Rising. Both captured, with James executed at the Tower of London. Charles escaped but later joined the 1745 uprising and met the same fate.
The Next Chapter of Restoration
The next chapter began in 1882, historian Cadwallader Bates purchased the property and restored it to its 14th‑century splendour. After his death in 1902, his wife Josephine continued, rebuilding the rooftop chapel with permission from Pope Leo XIII. Remaining dedicated to the restoration until her death in 1933 and was buried beside him in the grounds.
After Josephine’s passing, the Castle stood empty until the Second World War, when it served as military barracks. It later became a girls’ boarding school, operating until around 1972.
The Greenwich Hospital Era
After the execution of James Radcliffe, 3rd Earl of Derwentwater (and his brother) and the forfeiture of the estate, it was taken by the Crown and handed over to the governors of Greenwich Hospital in 1749. The lands and associated income-generating assets were managed, but the castle itself was largely neglected, and remained in a state of ruin for more than a century.
Restoration and Renewal
The castle was purchased in 1986 by Dr Stuart Madnick, a professor at MIT. He restored and renovated the building, transforming it into the luxury hotel it is today.
Battlements Tours - Join our Battlement Tour at 10:15 am daily. It explores the Castle’s original structure, historic owners and reveals hidden features at the top of the battlements.

wikipedia.title: Langley Castle
wikipedia.extract: Langley Castle is a restored medieval tower house, in the village of Langley in the valley of the River South Tyne. The castle is 3 miles (5 km) south of Haydon Bridge, in Northumberland, England. Langley Castle is a Grade I listed building. The property switched ownership several times over hundreds of years until Langley Castle was finally built in 1364. The castle was built in an H shape with four floors, and has four towers on each corner. The castle has several other unique architectural features. After being severely damaged by a fire in 1405, Langley Castle was left in ruins for 500 years until it was restored in 1914. In the last 100 years Langley Castle went through many uses, and now operates as a hotel.
